newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe climbs in opinion poll.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe climbs in opinion poll.

text.p: The public image of French Prime Minister Alain Juppe has improved sharply from record lows, according to an opinion poll released on Wednesday.
The IFOP survey said that 40 percent of voters had confidence in the centre-right premier, up from 31 percent last December.
The standing of President Jacques Chirac also rose, to 47 percent from 44, according to the poll of 950 voters to be published on Thursday in the news weekly L'Express.
Juppe's popularity had plunged to record lows amid popular discontent over acute unemployment and austerity budget policies aimed at helping France qualify for European monetary union.
His standing has been recovering as economic prospects brightened and after he published a first-person book aimed at humanising his image.
